# LeadLab Deployment Synthesis

**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent)

Consolidates: `deployment-method.md`, `email-delivery.md`, `monitoring-logging.md`, `queue-scheduler.md`, `backup-restore.md`, `dokploy-vs-coolify.md` (all dated 2026-08-30).

## 1. Executive summary

Six areas were researched for deploying Laravel 13 + Inertia/React on a single 8 GB Proxmox VM with SQLite: deployment platform, CI/CD, email, queue/scheduler, monitoring, and backup. The recommended stack is **Coolify** (self-hosted, $0) on one Debian 13 VM, fed by **GitHub Actions** builds pushed to **GHCR**, with **Amazon SES** for email (~$0.50/mo), the **SQLite database queue driver on a dedicated queue file with exactly one worker**, a self-hosted monitoring blend (Uptime Kuma + GlitchTip + Loki/Grafana + Prometheus, $0), and a layered backup strategy (Litestream + spatie/laravel-backup to the Synology NAS, plus Proxmox Backup Server for whole-VM restores). Total additional cost is **~$1/mo**, worst case ~$7/mo with an optional offsite S3 bucket - far under the $50 budget.

|---|---|---|
| Deployment platform | **Coolify** (self-hosted) on Debian 13 Proxmox VM | 4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM / 60 GB NVMe + second vdisk for `/var/lib/docker/volumes`. Compose-as-source-of-truth, official Laravel docs, GitHub App auto-deploy, one-click rollback. Fit score 4.6/5 vs Dokploy (viable, better registry rollback but no Laravel docs) and CapRover (3.7, Swarm friction). |
| CI/CD method | **GitHub Actions -> GHCR -> Coolify pulls prebuilt image** | Push to `main` triggers test (`php artisan test`, `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`) + multi-stage Docker build (~180-220 MB image) + push `ghcr.io/ssd-org/leadlab:<sha>`. Coolify deploys by pulling - no build load on the 8 GB VM. `php artisan migrate --force` as pre-deploy command, runs once. Rollback: Coolify one-click (prior local image) or `IMAGE_TAG=<old-sha>`. |
| Email delivery | **Amazon SES**, native Laravel `ses` driver, region `eu-west-1` | HTTPS API (no SMTP egress port). ~$0.10/1,000 emails; 3,000-8,000/mo volume = **~$0.30-0.80/mo**. Production quota ~50k/day, ~14 msg/sec clears a 200-person reminder burst in ~15 s (M365's 30/min throttle would take ~7 min). M365 SMTP rejected as primary: Basic auth EOL by late Dec 2026. Runner-up: Brevo $9/mo Starter. |
| Queue driver | **Laravel `database` driver on a dedicated `queue.sqlite` file, ONE worker container** | `sqlite_queue` connection, WAL + `busy_timeout=10000`, `after_commit => true`. One worker: 60-300 emails/min (SMTP-bound), 3x headroom over peak. Never add a second worker against SQLite (`database is locked` + duplicate-send risk). Redis + Horizon is the documented one-line upgrade path when a 2nd node or Horizon is wanted. **Note:** `deployment-method.md` sketched Redis queue + 2 workers; the specialist queue research overrides this for SQLite (see Open decisions). |
| Scheduler approach | **Dedicated `php artisan schedule:work` container** | No host cron. Missed ticks are absorbed by a window-based `reminders:dispatch` sweep: `everyMinute()->withoutOverlapping(5)->onOneServer()`, 180-min catch-up floor, `event_reminders` idempotency ledger with `UNIQUE(calendar_event_id, offset_label)` and conditional-UPDATE claiming. `stop_grace_period: 65s` on the worker so in-flight jobs finish. |
| Monitoring stack | **Uptime Kuma 2.5 + GlitchTip v6 + Loki 3/Alloy + Prometheus + Grafana; Better Stack free as external watchdog; spatie/laravel-health in-app** | $0, ~2-4 GB RAM. Kuma: `/up` + `/health` checks, push heartbeats for scheduler + queue, TLS expiry (21-day warn). GlitchTip: Sentry-SDK-compatible, ~512 MB, DSN swap for hosted Sentry later. Loki: 30-day retention (`retention_period: 720h`), alert on `SQLITE_BUSY` rate. Prometheus alerts: 5xx rate >5%, queue backlog >500, SQLite volume <15% free. Telescope: non-prod only (`Telescope::stopRecording()` in prod). Pulse optional (needs its own MariaDB/Redis connection - not SQLite). |
| Backup strategy | **Hybrid: Litestream (continuous) + spatie/laravel-backup (with `.backup` hook) -> Synology SFTP, + PBS whole-VM nightly** | Litestream: WAL frames to NAS every few seconds (RPO seconds). spatie: `--only-db` every 2 h, full nightly 01:30, retention 7d/16d/8w/4m/2y, AES-encrypted (zip holds `.env`), `backup:monitor` hourly. `BackupHasStarted` hook runs `sqlite3 .backup` so the zipped DB is transactionally consistent. PBS: nightly VM backup, prune 14d/8w/12m/2y, weekly verify - crash-consistent only, never the sole DB backup. RTO: DB ~10-20 min, whole VM 15-45 min, total-loss rebuild 30-45 min. |
| SSL/TLS | **Cloudflare Tunnel** (preferred) or Coolify's Traefik + Let's Encrypt **DNS-01** (fallback) | Tunnel: no inbound ports (outbound QUIC), TLS at edge, WAF + Zero-Trust for the internal audience; needs `CNAME leadlab.* -> <uuid>.cfargotunnel.com` approved by domain admins. Fallback works with 80/443 internal-only via `_acme-challenge` CNAME delegation. Both domains are a first-class field in Coolify. |

## 4. SQLite production constraints

SQLite is a single file with a **database-level write lock**. These rules are non-negotiable; violating any of them produces `database is locked` errors, duplicate reminder emails, or corrupt backups.

**What SQLite cannot do here:**
- **One writer, globally, at every instant.** WAL mode lets readers and writers coexist; it does **not** allow two writers. No `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` exists on SQLite, so multi-worker queue concurrency is unsupported by design.
- **No second app node.** Every process that opens the DB (app, queue worker, scheduler, `artisan` one-offs, Litestream) must run on the same host against the same volume. HA comes from Proxmox VM replication/HA (whole-VM), not app clustering.
- **No network filesystems.** The live DB must never sit on NFS/CIFS/SMB - locking and mmap break. The NAS is for backups only.
- **No naive file copies.** `cp`/`rsync`/`tar` of a live WAL-mode DB silently misses data in the `-wal` file or captures a torn copy. Proxmox/PBS snapshots are crash-consistent ("pulled the power"), not known-good.

**The rules:**

1. **Mount the directory, not the file.** The volume must hold all three files: `database.sqlite`, `-wal`, `-shm`. Named Docker volume on the NVMe-backed VM disk.
2. **Set the PRAGMAs in `config/database.php`** (Laravel 13 accepts them natively):
   ```php
   'sqlite' => [
       'driver' => 'sqlite',
       'database' => env('DB_DATABASE', '/var/www/db/database.sqlite'),
       'foreign_key_constraints' => true,
       'busy_timeout' => 5000,       // ms; wait instead of erroring
       'journal_mode' => 'WAL',      // readers never block the writer
       'synchronous' => 'NORMAL',    // safe with WAL
       'cache_size' => -20000,       // ~20 MB page cache
   ],
   'sqlite_queue' => [               // dedicated queue file
       'driver' => 'sqlite',
       'database' => database_path('queue.sqlite'),
       'busy_timeout' => 10000,
       'journal_mode' => 'WAL',
       'synchronous' => 'NORMAL',
   ],
   ```
3. **Keep churn off the main file.** Cache + session on Redis; queue jobs + `failed_jobs` on the separate `queue.sqlite`. Domain data only in `database.sqlite`.
4. **Exactly one queue worker.** `queue:work database --queue=reminders,default --sleep=1 --tries=3 --backoff=30 --max-time=3600 --timeout=60`, `stop_grace_period: 65s`, `--timeout` < `retry_after` (90 s). Treating >1 worker as unsupported.
5. **Run migrations once per deploy**, in the Coolify pre-deploy hook (`migrate --force`), never per replica. Keep migrations additive and reversible - a rollback does not undo a schema change.
6. **Checkpoint the WAL on a schedule.** `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` every 5-10 min as a scheduler task, so an always-attached reader can't grow `-wal` unbounded.
7. **Back up only via the Online Backup API.** `sqlite3 database.sqlite ".backup '/path/out.sqlite'"` or `VACUUM INTO` (needs >= 3.27) produce a transactionally consistent file while the app runs. Then verify with `PRAGMA integrity_check` and ship the inert copy anywhere (rsync/SFTP/NAS) safely.
8. **Never share the DB file across hosts or containers on different kernels.** WAL's shared-memory coordination requires same host + same filesystem.
9. **Capacity ceiling is far above this workload.** WAL-mode SQLite on NVMe handles hundreds of writes/sec; 50-200 users on a read-heavy Inertia app is comfortably within it. Contention signals (`SQLITE_BUSY` rate, WAL size) are monitored via Loki alerts and the `sqlite_db_size_bytes` Prometheus gauge.

## 6. What to build first

1. **Provision the Proxmox VM:** Debian 13, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 60 GB NVMe disk + a second virtual disk for `/var/lib/docker/volumes`, qemu-guest-agent installed, on a Proxmox HA group. Docker runs in a VM, not LXC.
2. **Harden the VM:** SSH keys only, unattended upgrades, swap enabled. Restrict SSH exposure for CI (GitHub IP allowlist, or self-hosted runner, or Cloudflare Tunnel for SSH).
3. **Install Coolify:** `curl -fsSL https://cdn.coollabs.io/coolify/install.sh | bash` (~3 min). Connect the GitHub App; set both domains (`leadlab.ssd.org`, `leadlab.adventist.asia`) on the app resource.
4. **Write the repo deployment files:** multi-stage Dockerfile (Node 22 asset build -> composer vendor -> `dunglas/frankenphp:1-php8.3-alpine` runtime with `pdo_sqlite pcntl opcache redis intl zip gd`), and `compose.yaml`: `app`, `queue` x1, `scheduler`, `redis` (cache/session), `litestream`, `cloudflared`, with named volumes `leadlab-db` -> `/var/www/db` and `leadlab-storage` -> `/var/www/html/storage/app`.
5. **Apply the SQLite config from section 4** in `config/database.php`; run `make:queue-table` / `make:queue-failed-table` against `sqlite_queue`; add the `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` scheduler task.
6. **Create the GitHub Actions workflow:** test job (php artisan test on SQLite `:memory:`, `npm run build`, `tsc --noEmit`), build job (buildx with GHA cache, push `<sha>` + `latest` to GHCR), deploy via Coolify webhook. Set the pre-deploy command `php artisan migrate --force`. Snapshot the VM before the first deploy.
7. **Set up SES:** create/request AWS org account, request SES production access (~24 h, describe transactional-only use + suppression handling), verify domain, add 3 Easy DKIM CNAMEs + custom MAIL FROM subdomain (`bounce.yourdomain.com` MX -> `feedback-smtp.eu-west-1.amazonses.com` + SPF TXT; root SPF stays pointed at M365), IAM user scoped to `ses:SendEmail` with a `FromAddress` condition, SNS -> Laravel webhook for bounces/complaints + suppression check before reminder sends, DMARC `p=none` initially. Keep mail on queues (`ShouldQueue`), dedicated `reminders` queue.
8. **Wire TLS:** if domain admins approve the CNAMEs, create the Cloudflare Tunnel and drop the token into `cloudflared`; otherwise configure Coolify's Traefik with Let's Encrypt DNS-01 using org DNS API creds.
9. **Stand up the monitoring compose project** (separate project, shared `web` network): Uptime Kuma (HTTP monitors on `/up` + `/health` keyword `"status":"ok"`, TLS monitor, two push monitors for scheduler + queue heartbeats), GlitchTip (+ Postgres + Valkey; create project, point `sentry/sentry-laravel` DSN at it), Loki + Alloy (Docker socket log shipping, multiline PHP stitching), Prometheus + node/cAdvisor + `spatie/laravel-prometheus` `/metrics` route (auth-protected), Grafana with the ~8 core alert rules. Register Better Stack free external monitor + scheduler heartbeat. Enable Cloudflare Web Analytics. Gate Telescope to non-prod.
10. **Build the backup layers:** `litestream.yml` replica to Synology MinIO (or `file://` on an NFS-mounted replica dir); spatie/laravel-backup with the `BackupHasStarted` -> `sqlite3 .backup` hook, `nas` SFTP disk (restricted NAS user, key auth), schedule `backup:clean` 01:00 / `--only-db` every 2 h / full 01:30 / `backup:monitor` hourly, `BACKUP_ARCHIVE_PASSWORD` set; PBS datastore on the NAS + nightly VM backup with prune (14d/8w/12m/2y) + weekly verify; enable NAS Btrfs snapshots + Hyper Backup offsite for 3-2-1.
11. **Implement the reminder pipeline:** `event_reminders` ledger (`UNIQUE(calendar_event_id, offset_label)`, `send_after`, `sent_at`), `reminders:dispatch` command scheduled `everyMinute()->withoutOverlapping(5)->onOneServer()` with a 180-min catch-up floor and `isPast()` guard, `SendEventReminder` queued job with `Cache::lock()` idempotency re-check. Add `Queue::failing()` alert hook + weekly `queue:prune-failed`.
12. **Prove recovery before go-live:** run the nightly restore-test script (pull from NAS, `integrity_check`, table/user/migration counts, dead-man's-switch ping), do one manual full VM restore drill to a scratch VMID, and write the restore runbook (including where `.env`/APP_KEY copies live).

## 7. Open decisions

| # | Decision | Why it blocks implementation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Cloudflare Tunnel CNAME approval** - will the `ssd.org` / `adventist.asia` domain admins allow `CNAME leadlab.* -> <uuid>.cfargotunnel.com`? | Determines the TLS path (Tunnel vs Traefik DNS-01) and whether firewall changes are needed. Ask before step 8. |
| 2 | **AWS account + SES production access** - org policy on an external processor for participant email; confirm EU region (`eu-west-1` vs `eu-central-1`) per GDPR posture; execute AWS DPA. | SES is the email pick; production access takes ~24 h and needs a use description. Org privacy sign-off may be required. |
| 3 | **Queue driver confirmation** - the specialist queue research (`database` driver, dedicated `queue.sqlite`, 1 worker) and the deployment-method sketch (Redis, 2 workers) conflict; this synthesis follows the specialist research. | One-line confirmation avoids rework. Redis is already in the stack for cache/session, so switching to `QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis` + Horizon later is cheap if the team prefers it. |
| 4 | **Hybrid mailer for admin alerts** - must internal admin registration alerts stay inside the M365 trust boundary (Direct Send / Graph), or is all-via-SES acceptable? | Adds a second sender identity + failure mode if required. Only worth it if org policy demands it. |
| 5 | **Alert routing** - who is on-call, and to which channel (phone/SMS via Better Stack free, Telegram, Slack, email)? Severity thresholds (critical = phone, warning = email). | Monitoring cannot be finished without a destination; avoids alert fatigue by design. |
| 6 | **Laravel Pulse adoption** - needs its own MariaDB container (~RAM) on the 8 GB VM, since Pulse storage does not support SQLite. | Optional nice-to-have; decide based on remaining RAM headroom after the monitoring stack (~4.5-5 GB projected total, ~3 GB free). |
| 7 | **Offsite backup leg** - weekly rclone of snapshots to M365 SharePoint ($0, uses owned tenant) vs a $5-6/mo B2/R2 bucket. | Both satisfy 3-2-1; pick one so Hyper Backup config can be finalized. |

## 8. Risk register

| # | Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **SQLite write-lock contention** - `database is locked` errors or duplicate reminder emails when queue, web writes, and migrations collide on one file | Dedicated `queue.sqlite` with `after_commit`; exactly one worker (never scale to 2); WAL + `busy_timeout` 5000/10000 ms; idempotency ledger + conditional-UPDATE claiming for reminders; Loki alert on `SQLITE_BUSY` rate; Redis+Horizon upgrade path documented. |
| 2 | **Bad deploy or destructive migration** - rollback restores code but not schema/data; Coolify rollback only works with locally retained images | Pre-deploy VM snapshot + Proxmox snapshot of the DB volume disk; `migrate --force` runs once as a pre-deploy hook; keep migrations additive/reversible; Coolify one-click rollback to prior build; Litestream gives point-in-time DB restore (RPO seconds). |
| 3 | **Backups exist but don't restore** - torn WAL copies, silent corruption, untested restore paths | Only `.backup`/`VACUUM INTO`/Litestream, never bare file copies of a live DB; `PRAGMA integrity_check` on every snapshot; nightly automated restore-test from the NAS copy wired to a dead-man's switch; `backup:monitor` hourly + failure notifications; quarterly full-VM restore drill with recorded RTO. |
| 4 | **Single-VM or node outage blinds both the app and self-hosted monitoring** | Better Stack free external watchdog (sees the outage from outside); Proxmox HA group + VM replication (few-minutes RTO); PBS nightly backup for full-VM restore (15-45 min); optionally a second Uptime Kuma on the Synology so a cluster-wide failure still has a live monitor. |
| 5 | **Email failure** - SES stuck in sandbox, deliverability drops, or M365 Basic-auth EOL (late Dec 2026) breaks an SMTP-based fallback | Request SES production access during setup (week 1, not at launch); Easy DKIM + MAIL FROM subdomain + DMARC monitoring; SNS bounce/complaint webhook + account-level suppression list; dedicated `reminders` queue so mail never blocks other work; synthetic hourly send test with heartbeat; M365 used only for internal alerts via Direct Send/Graph, never Basic-auth SMTP. |
